profiles.Summary: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a visually ambitious Unreal Engine 5 turn-based RPG whose PC minimum spec (GTX 1060) sits just above the Steam Deck's GPU class, meaning the Deck can run it but needs reduced settings and FSR upscaling to stay smooth. The game is Steam Deck Verified and runs natively under Proton with full controller support, though demanding combat and open areas will stress the hardware.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB player reports were available at time of writing; all three profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 class) versus Deck GPU capability (GTX 1050 Ti class) and general UE5 behaviour on the hardware. On first boot, check the frame rate in the opening area and during your first combat encounter — if you see sustained dips below 30 fps on Optimal, drop to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR reconstruct to 1280x800; the 8 W TDP and locked GPU clock keep heat and draw low for long sessions. Turn-based gameplay makes 30 fps feel perfectly acceptable here.

UE5 titles often exhibit shader compilation stutters on first play; expect hitching until shaders are cached.
High-fidelity UE5 features (Lumen, Nanite) are likely too demanding for the Deck GPU at any quality level.
Shared memory bandwidth between CPU and GPU on the Deck's APU can bottleneck UE5 titles, so RAM-heavy settings (shadows, textures) should be kept low.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP unlocked targets 60 fps but the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU will struggle in dense areas, expect dips to the low 40s; consider dropping to 40 fps cap if frame time variance becomes distracting. Battery life is short — best used plugged in or for short sessions.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 fps / 40 Hz lock on the OLED panel is the sweet spot — it feels smooth, holds within the Deck's power budget, and the turn-based combat pacing makes occasional dips to 36 fps barely noticeable. Raise shadow and effects quality one step at a time if headroom allows.
